title: Corsair-class inference silicon books a named hyperscaler deployment by Q3 2027
body: d-Matrix's June 9 announcement that its Corsair inference accelerator has entered full production and is shipping in volume to priority customers is the clearest sign yet that a non-GPU inference entrant has reached deployable scale. Corsair is built on a digital in-memory-compute (DIMC) chiplet architecture that fuses SRAM and compute on-die and pairs it with LPDDR5 on TSMC's N6 node, attacking the memory-bandwidth wall that throttles transformer decoding on conventional GPUs; alongside it, d-Matrix shipped SquadRack, a rack-scale reference design built with Arista, Broadcom, and Supermicro that packages Corsair cards into a production-ready inference rack rather than a bare accelerator. The company cites independent Gimlet Labs testing showing a disaggregated setup cutting a 24-second baseline response to under two seconds (roughly 12x latency improvement on that workload) and broader claims of about 10x faster, 3x cheaper, and up to 5x more energy-efficient inference versus a standalone GPU when Corsair fronts a Blackwell host; Microsoft is among its backers, and it says about 90 percent of customers are US-based. This is the structural moment the standing thesis predicts - that purpose-built inference silicon fills the market gap left by GPU-only economics - but a volume ship to unnamed priority customers is not yet proof of franchise; it could stall at design-win pilots that never convert to scaled production. The forward thesis is that the in-memory-compute category crosses from production launch into a named, at-scale commercial deployment. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by Q3 2027 at least one named hyperscaler, neocloud, or large enterprise publicly commits Corsair-class non-GPU inference silicon (d-Matrix Corsair/SquadRack, or a second digital-in-memory-compute entrant reaching volume) to a production deployment at scale - confirmed via an on-record customer announcement naming the operator and the workload, a signed multi-rack purchase or capacity disclosure, or a disclosed revenue/units milestone tied to a named buyer. A continued stream of unnamed priority-customer shipments, a benchmark or pilot press release, an evaluation that never converts, or a packaging/partnership-only deal does not count; the marker is a named operator running this class of in-memory-compute silicon in production at scale. The counter-risk is that the workloads stay GPU-bound on software-ecosystem inertia and CUDA tooling, leaving Corsair-class parts in pilot and niche deployments while the named at-scale wins go to merchant GPUs.

reasoning.because: Corsair (SRAM in-memory-compute, TSMC N6) entered full production June 9, shipping in volume
reasoning.given: the GPU memory-bandwidth wall throttles decoding; Microsoft-backed DIMC now ships at rack scale
reasoning.so_that: a named hyperscaler/neocloud/large enterprise commits Corsair-class non-GPU inference silicon to production scale
reasoning.landing: by Q3 2027; >=1 named hyperscaler/neocloud Corsair-class production deployment
reasoning.plain_language: d-Matrix now sells a non-GPU AI inference chip in volume; soon a big named cloud will run it in production at scale.

summary: d-Matrix moved its Corsair inference accelerator into full production on June 9 and shipped the rack-scale SquadRack, the clearest sign a non-GPU SRAM in-memory-compute design has reached deployable scale. Expect a named hyperscaler or neocloud to deploy Corsair-class silicon by Q3 2027.
